purpose: Bolder concept alternatives requested after rejection of generic courtyard layouts. Every alternative contains an enclosed equipment room. Concept only, no map changes.

variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: bold final game environment art concept for an old prison factory courtyard.
Image 1 is the original Godot map screenshot, authoritative neighborhood geometry. The three red rectangles mark the connected southeast courtyard: existing tree garden at top center, empty south court east of laundry, pocket south of warehouse. Image 2 is a previous proposal and STYLE reference only. The user explicitly REJECTED its generic arrangement as boring. Do not just re-place the same benches, pergola and small rectangular room. Create a dramatically different memorable spatial composition with a strong industrial architectural idea, a clear focal point and deliberate circulation. Stay credible for an aged factory prison campus. Buildings and ground organization can change boldly WITHIN the marked empty district, but retain existing kiosk at upper-left, tree-and-monument garden at upper-middle, laundry/bath at left, long warehouse at right, their doors, and CLOSED exterior southern stone wall. No new outside exit. Keep a broad usable east-west service road just inside the southern wall and a traversable north-south route from upper garden to it. Respect game scale and door clearances.
Include an actual enclosed equipment room of meaningful size, with pale stone walls, weathered teal lower walls, usable door gap, and plaque "设备间". Show its interior using the SAME orthographic roof-off convention as existing visible buildings: tank, pump, electrical control panels, red/blue pipe runs, clear service aisle. Room feels integrated into the architectural concept. Roof visibility is lifted for the equipment room; outdoor canopies can retain their roofs. No front-elevation door pasted into a sidewall. No hard disconnected dark rectangular floor artifacts. Avoid a generic tiny square utility box surrounded by random benches. Infrastructure is purposeful, weathered and visually striking, not dangerous heaps, fantasy machines or a pristine resort.
Style: high-quality coherent hand-painted 2D game sprites, orthographic overhead camera with only modest visible front edges consistent with reference, muted olive/cream stone/steel blue/rust/ochre, detailed masonry, faded markings, believable subtle shadows. No isometric camera, photoreal architecture rendering or dramatic perspective. Design is readable in gameplay at small scale. Include 3 small orange prisoner sprites and 1 navy guard on clear paths for scale. Existing perimeter wall reads continuous at the bottom.
Frame one polished landscape 3:2 final concept image zoomed into the ENTIRE redesigned district, narrow contextual slices of laundry left and warehouse right. No editor UI, red boxes or selection dots. Add a neat cream caption strip below the map with exact variant title. No other diagram arrows or explanatory text.
VARIANT SEVEN — caption exactly "方案七 · 管线能源庭院".
Architectural idea: a powerful irregular L-shaped equipment building wraps the SOUTHWEST corner of the empty court, with two connected enclosed wings, roof lifted to reveal a tall horizontal pressure vessel in the west wing and pump/control bank in the south wing. The L-shaped room is integrated, not two unconnected boxes. An eye-catching low overhead RED AND BLUE PIPE GANTRY extends from this service building toward the warehouse along the EAST side of the court, on several stout steel posts with clear passage UNDER it. Keep supports outside walking route and do not obscure the tree garden. Build a single large broken-octagonal industrial service island in the center-right: a low circular valve/inspection platform, patterned paving ring, blue maintenance rail only on its rear half, and warm yellow-black service markings, around which walking paths curve visibly. One of the red pipes bends down into this island. The upper tree garden remains green and calm, connected to the courtyard by a slightly curved stone-bordered path. Use a few asymmetric ivy/grass patches clinging to walls and one pair of benches near the kiosk; NO pergola, NO chess table, NO row of identical recycling bins. Replace most of the uniform tile monotony with a compelling mix of worn concrete, curved tile path and rusty service apron. The composition should look like the visual centerpiece of the factory's working infrastructure, not a generic park. Leave the bottom through-road open.

VARIANT EIGHT — caption exactly "方案八 · 水渠锅炉院".
Architectural idea: a compact old boiler/pump room in the SOUTHEAST pocket uses an angled/chamfered corner rather than a plain rectangular box. Roof-off room shows one distinctive horizontal cylindrical boiler, copper-red heat pipes, blue pump bank and control panels. Its west-facing door opens into the courtyard and remains legible in overhead wall orientation. From this room a NARROW shallow industrial cooling/drainage channel with visible muted green water winds diagonally across the lower courtyard toward laundry, with stone/concrete edges and 2 short blue steel footbridges at crossings. Channel is shallow, enclosed and clearly manufactured for drainage, not a swimming pool or deep moat; ALL routes remain connected using bridges wide enough for gameplay. Design the southwest area as a triangular weathered cobble terrace with one large mature shade tree, a curved low brick planter/seat wall and a couple of plain timber seats. Between channel and old tree garden place an irregular island of moss, coarse grass and worn service covers; vegetation makes the infrastructure feel decades old. Along the boiler-room edge include two blue barrels and hose reel, not crate clutter. Keep outdoor spaces open and strong diagonal composition visually balances the rectilinear buildings. No pergola or generic chess table. A memorable damp industrial courtyard with water, stone, pipe and shade, still a prison factory, not an ornamental luxury garden. Preserve broad southern road.

VARIANT NINE — caption exactly "方案九 · 围合维修院".
Architectural idea: a large OPEN U-shaped service court occupies the SOUTHWEST/MIDDLE empty district; three sides are built differently: north wing a roof-off enclosed equipment room with real machinery and clear aisle, west side a narrow sawtooth corrugated-roof repair arcade attached to that wing, south side a low tool/parts counter and partial waist-high masonry wall. The U opens widely EAST toward the warehouse/main route. This is NOT a closed tall-walled compound that traps walking. Give the inner repair court a distinctive ochre worn concrete floor with a central work hoist/low engine stand, one rolling service cart and long benches under arcade. Equipment-room door opens into this court, labelled "设备间". A narrow planted edge with vines and a modest mature tree marks the outer west side. In the SOUTHEAST pocket, introduce an asymmetric triangular wedge of lawn bordered with small stones, one long curved wooden bench and a single lamp, opposing the angular mechanical U-court. The existing upper tree garden stays as its own focal point; connect it to the U opening via a generous winding gray tiled pedestrian route. Place one prisoner repairing at a table and others walking. No random crate piles, no repeating bins or square lawn islands. The new architecture creates a strong place with layered roofs, visible equipment and an inhabitable central working courtyard. Keep broad south service road between U structure and exterior wall completely open.
